text: {"observations":"A continuous, nearly constant noise fills the whole 10 s: the loudness envelope sits at the top level throughout and the band profile is almost identical in every 0.25 s step, with noisiness 7-8. It has a stable hump around 500-800 Hz (peaks near 650-700 Hz) and a persistent narrow ridge near 6.75 kHz, while the 0-125 Hz band is weak. That steady, resonant character with little low-frequency energy and no gusting fits a machine/mechanism hum better than wind, which would normally be low-frequency heavy and fluctuating; this is an inference, not a certainty. The only other events are short: extra energy at about 3.2-4.4 s and 8.0-9.0 s in the 1-1.5 kHz, 2-3 kHz and 4-6 kHz bands, consistent with brief vocal sounds (meow or voice) lasting about 1 s each, far shorter than the background. This rules out C and D as longest and favours A over B.","answer":"A"}
